question_stem:
Fig. 10.1 shows a simple laminated iron-cored transformer consisting of a primary coil of 25000 turns and a secondary coil of 625 turns.
{{figure:figure_10_1}}
Fig. 10.1
The output potential difference (p.d.) $V_{OUT}$ is applied to a load resistor of resistance $640\,\Omega$.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State the function of the iron core.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the iron core is laminated.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem: The input p.d. $V_{IN}$ is a sinusoidal alternating voltage of peak value $12\text{kV}$ and period $40\text{ms}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) current in the load resistor.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
(c)
parts.text: Explain, with reference to Fig.10.2, why the mean power in the load resistor is $70\text{W}$.
